title: Watermark-driven KV sharding and predictive prefill prioritization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Our paged KV architecture maintains variable-size pages per shard. As models and traffic patterns diversify, we see uneven hotset skew across shards and costly mid-request prefill stalls when the serving runtime chooses to fetch large remote pages during decode. Problem: Current allocation/eviction uses simple LRU heuristics by page last-access; this leads to (1) cross-shard imbalance where a few hot shards consume disproportionate resident memory, (2) noisy eviction thrashing on bursty chat sessions, and (3) suboptimal prefill ordering — prefill tasks treat all candidate pages equally and may fetch low-value prefixes ahead of near-term decode needs. Goal: Reduce tail latency and memory churn by introducing a watermark-driven sharding policy (per-shard soft/hard watermarks + inter-shard rebalancer) and a predictive prefill prioritizer that ranks page prefetches by sequence-aware urgency. Scope: runtime KV manager, prefill scheduler, small changes to shard metadata and metrics. No public API changes. Proposal summary: 1) Watermark-driven sharding: each KV shard gets a dynamic soft and hard resident-page watermark based on recent request mix and per-shard token-rate. Soft watermark triggers cooperative rebalancing: low-priority pages (coldly scored) are migrated to less-loaded shards or compacted to free contiguous slots. Hard watermark forces eviction/compaction and signals fallback to smaller model variants for that customer when eviction would otherwise violate latency SLOs. 2) Predictive prefill prioritization: compute a per-prefill score = w1 * imminence_estimate + w2 * access_frequency + w3 * continuity_score (how likely subsequent requests will continue the same context). Imminence is estimated from request route metadata + user session activity decay. Continuity_score uses short-term seq ID heuristics. Prefill worker consumes a priority queue; low-score items are deprioritized or batched into background compaction. 3) Fragmentation mitigation pass (vacuum): periodic lightweight slot defragmenter that coalesces small free slots to reduce allocation search time and improve locality for GPU kernels. 4) Kernel selection hints: expose a small hint from the shard manager to the kernel selector indicating expected average sequence-length for the busiest shard window so the kernel chooser prefers low-overhead attention kernels when sequences are short. Trade-offs: - Migration and compaction cost CPU/GPU cycles; keep vacuuming rate adaptive to load. - Hard watermark fallback nudges product decisions (model variant fallback): requires coordination with routing/fallback policy. - Prefill scoring introduces heuristics; we'll instrument and A/B test weights. Implementation plan: - Phase 1 (design + prototypes): implement per-shard watermarks and prefill scoring in a feature-flagged branch; add metrics (resident_pages, soft_watermark_pct, eviction_forced_count, prefill_queue_score_distribution). - Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of traffic, monitor tail latency, eviction rates, and memory usage. - Phase 3 (rollout): expand to 50% then 100% with automatic throttles for compaction. Backward compatibility: feature-flag ensures fallback to existing LRU behavior. Observability: dashboards and alerts: "kv.watermark.violation" and alert when forced evictions spike > 3x baseline. Links: design doc: https://docs.redwood/products/runtime/watermark-kv-shards, draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5342
acceptance_criteria: Resident memory imbalance across shards (p95 shard resident_pages / mean) reduced by >= 30% on synthetic skewed workload
Median decode tail latency (p99) from KV fetch stalls reduced by >= 20% on bursty session trace
Forced eviction events during normal traffic < 0.5 per 1000 requests after adaptive tuning
Prefill hit-rate for near-term decode windows increases by >= 15% (measured over chat session traces)
Feature gated with clear rollback; dashboard and alerts in place prior to canary
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in prod initially
Enable for internal loadtests and batch synthetic workloads
Canary: 5% user traffic for 48h, monitor metrics and latency traces
If stable, ramp to 50% over 24h; if any kv.watermark.violation alert fires, rollback immediately
Full rollout after 7-day burn and tuning of vacuum rate
implementation_notes: Add per-shard watermark state to runtime/kv/shard_state.cc (lightweight counters + EWMA token rate)
Prefill priority queue in runtime/prefill/scheduler.go with PluggableScorer interface
Vacuum compactor as a low-priority background worker pinned to utility cores to avoid interfering with decode
Kernel hint bridge: runtime/kernel_selector.h add optional expected_seq_len_hint to selector API
Bench harness: reuse existing paged-attention traces in infra/perf-tests; new synthetic skew generator in infra/benchmark to validate balance
PR checklist: unit tests for scoring, integration test for migration path, perf test comparing memory and p99 latency
